evidence.quote: Our conclusion concerns the smooth positive-density version; we do not assert an obstruction for every equivalent-to-volume invariant measure.

exclusions.query: Obstruction to every invariant measure equivalent to volume
exclusions.reason: Equivalence to volume alone does not supply the strictly positive smooth density used in the switch estimate.

evidence.quote: Full support does not require a smooth positive density.

exclusions.query: Obstruction to all smooth full-support invariant-measure models
exclusions.reason: Full support is weaker than a smooth positive density and is explicitly distinguished from the obstructed regime.

evidence.quote: There exists an ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformation $(X,\mu,T)$ of a standard nonatomic probability space such that $h_\mu(T)=0$ and $(X,\mu,T)$ is not measurably conjugate, on invariant conull sets, to any $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a compact finite-dimensional manifold preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density.

exclusions.query: A finite algorithm deciding whether arbitrary zero-entropy systems have smooth models
exclusions.reason: The main result constructs an existential counterexample; it gives no general decision procedure for arbitrary input systems.

evidence.quote: Lind and Thouvenot realized finite-entropy ergodic transformations by Lebesgue-preserving homeomorphisms of the two-torus (Lind and Thouvenot 1977)

exclusions.query: Nonexistence of homeomorphic realizations for all finite-entropy systems
exclusions.reason: The introduction records a positive homeomorphic realization result, while the new obstruction imposes smoothness and smooth positive density.

outputs.exact_statement: There exists an ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformation $(X,\mu,T)$ of a standard nonatomic probability space such that $h_\mu(T)=0$ and $(X,\mu,T)$ is not measurably conjugate, on invariant conull sets, to any $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a compact finite-dimensional manifold preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density. The manifold may have smooth boundary and need not be orientable.

Fix $d\geq1$ and $A_*>1$. There is a constant $C$, depending only on these two quantities, with the following properties. Let $n\geq2$, $b>0$, and $\ln(2n+1)\leq bn$. Suppose that $A_t$, $-n\leq t<n$, are upper triangular with positive diagonal and $$\|A_t\|,\ \|A_t^{-1}\|\leq A_*,
 \qquad
 \left|\sum_{t=-n}^{u-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj}
                  -(u+n)\lambda_j\right|\leq bn$$ for $-n\leq u\leq n$ and $1\leq j\leq d$, where $\lambda_j=(2n)^{-1}\sum_{t=-n}^{n-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj}$.*


*First, order the rates as $\lambda_{(1)}\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_{(d)}$. For every $0\leq q\leq d$ and every $-n\leq s\leq t\leq n$, $$\label{eq:exterior-rate-comparison}
 \left|\ln\|\mathord{\bigwedge}^q A(t,s)\|
       -(t-s)\sum_{j=1}^q\lambda_{(j)}\right|\leq Cbn.$$ The analogous estimate for $A(s,t)$ uses the $q$ largest members of $\{-\lambda_1,\ldots,-\lambda_d\}$.*





*Next, suppose that real $\gamma$ and $g>0$ separate all the rates: each $\lambda_j$ is at most $\gamma-g$ or at least $\gamma+g$. Let $F$ be the set of indices in the second group, let $p=|F|$, and put $$\Lambda=\sum_{j\in F}\lambda_j,\qquad
 \Omega=-\sum_{j\notin F}\lambda_j.$$ There are decompositions $\mathbb R^d=E_t^s\oplus E_t^f$, $-n\leq t\leq n$, invariant under each $A_t$, with $\dim E_t^f=p$, whose two projections have norm at most $e^{Cbn}$. For $s\leq t$ and $l=t-s$ they satisfy $$\begin{aligned}
 \|A(t,s)|E_s^s\|&\leq e^{(\gamma-g)l+Cbn},
 &
 \|A(s,t)|E_t^f\|&\leq e^{-(\gamma+g)l+Cbn},
 \label{eq:split-propagation}\\
 \|\mathord{\bigwedge}^p A(t,s)\|&\leq e^{\Lambda l+Cbn},
 &
 e^{\Lambda l-Cbn}\leq
 J_p(A(t,s)|E_s^f)&\leq e^{\Lambda l+Cbn},
 \label{eq:fast-volume}\\
 \|\mathord{\bigwedge}^{d-p} A(s,t)\|&\leq e^{\Omega l+Cbn},
 &
 e^{\Omega l-Cbn}\leq
 J_{d-p}(A(s,t)|E_t^s)&\leq e^{\Omega l+Cbn}.
 \label{eq:slow-backward-volume}
\end{aligned}$$ If $0<p<d$ and at least one of $v_1,\ldots,v_p$ belongs to $E_s^s$, then $$\label{eq:mixed-exterior}
 \|A(t,s)v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge A(t,s)v_p\|
 \leq e^{(\Lambda-2g)l+Cbn}\prod_{j=1}^p\|v_j\|.$$ The backward analogue has exterior degree $d-p$, exponent $(\Omega-2g)l+Cbn$, and at least one factor in $E_t^f$. When a group is empty its space is $\{0\}$, all statements on that space are vacuous, and the exterior-degree-zero conventions apply.

For all sufficiently large $k$, each spatial bin $U$ meeting $\mathcal G_k$ has a number $$\gamma_U\in[g,(8d+1)g]$$ such that every good witness frame over $U$ has all its rates at most $\gamma_U-g$ or at least $\gamma_U+g$, with the same number $p_U$ in the second group. Apply [prop:finite-splitting](#prop:finite-splitting) using this threshold. There is $c>0$, independent of the bin and the witnesses, such that:* 1. *The spaces $E_0^s$ from any two good witnesses over $U$ are within $e^{-c gL}$ of one another in its coordinate chart. The same holds for the spaces $E_0^f$.* 2. *For good paths starting in $U$ whose time-$n$ endpoints lie in a common endpoint bin $V$, their spaces $E_n^f$ are within $e^{-c gL}$ of one another in the chart of $V$. For paths whose time-$(-n)$ endpoints lie in a common bin, the same assertion holds for $E_{-n}^s$.* *In particular, fix one representative space for each nonempty combination of bins in (ii). Orthogonal projection onto it, restricted to any corresponding actual endpoint space, is an isomorphism with inverse norm at most $2$. If $p_U=0$ or $p_U=d$, the relevant zero or full spaces agree exactly.

All four derivatives $DH_{xx}(x)$, $DH_{yy}(y)$, $DH_{xy}(z)$, and $DH_{yx}(w)$ are nonsingular. Locally the equations [eq:four-switch-equations] define a smooth pair map $\Phi(x,y)=(z,w)$ with $$\label{eq:pair-jacobian} J_{\nu\otimes\nu}\Phi(x,y)=1+o(1),$$ uniformly on the retained pairs. The conclusion includes empty slow or fast groups.

The map $\Phi:G_k\to M\times M$, $\Phi(x,y)=(z,w)$, is measurable and injective. Its restriction to countably many measurable pieces agrees with smooth local diffeomorphisms having the Jacobian in [eq:pair-jacobian].

Let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_q$ be independent random probability vectors on a set of cardinality $A$, all with mean $p$. Then $$\mathbb E\,\mathop{\mathrm{TV}}\left(\frac1q\sum_{b=1}^qY_b,p\right)
     \le\frac12\sqrt{\frac Aq}.$$ Coordinates within an individual vector need not be independent.

For the families in [prop:words](#prop:words), put $$d_i=\prod_{j=1}^{i-1}(1-\varepsilon_j),\qquad
 d_*=\prod_{j=1}^{\infty}(1-\varepsilon_j)>0.$$ Distinct $v,w\in\mathcal W_i$ satisfy $$d_{\mathrm H}(v,w)\ge d_i m_i\ge d_*m_i.$$ For all $v,w,z\in\mathcal W_i$ and every $1\le t<m_i$, $$d_{\mathrm H}\bigl((vw)[t,t+m_i),z\bigr)
     \ge d_i m_i\ge d_*m_i.$$ These distances count symbols in $\mathcal A$, and repeated source words are allowed.
There is a $T$-invariant ergodic Borel probability $\mu$ on $X$. Every $T$-invariant Borel probability on $X$ is nonatomic, is standard modulo null sets, and has zero Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy.

Let $2\le D\le D_i^*$ be a power of two and set $n=m_iD$. For all sufficiently large $i$, with $\mu$-probability at least $$1-\alpha_{i,D},\qquad
 \alpha_{i,D}=\frac{2D-2}{H_i},$$ all corresponding entries of $\mathcal L_{i,D}(x,-n)$ and $\mathcal L_{i,D}(x,0)$ pass the level-$i$ graph test simultaneously. In particular $\sup_{D\le D_i^*}\alpha_{i,D}\to0$.

Let $L=2^{2s}-1$ and equip the nonzero vectors of $\mathbb F_2^{2s}$ with a nondegenerate alternating form. Suppose a family of pairs of laws $(p_\xi,q_\xi)$ on these vectors is indexed by a probability space, and $$\mathbb E_\xi H(p_\xi)\ge .99\log L,\qquad
 \mathbb E_\xi H(q_\xi)\ge .99\log L.$$ For all sufficiently large $L$, independent samples from the two laws, followed by averaging over $\xi$, pass the test $[u,v]=0$ with probability at most $.62$.
